newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end lower; Nasdaq snaps winning streak.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end lower; Nasdaq snaps winning streak.

text.p: Wall Street paused in its record-shattering run Thursday, pulling blue-chip stocks slightly lower and sending Nasdaq to its first loss in two weeks.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended off 18.11 points to close at 8,020.77, as investors took profits after the previous day's rally pushed the Dow Jones industrial average above 8,000 points for the first time ever.
The Nasdaq index lost 11.78 points to 1,568.85, its first lower finish after 10 straight record highs.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,582 to 1,290 on heavy volume of 629 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"We needed this, we needed room to breathe," said Arnie Owen, managing director of capital markets at Cruttenden Roth. "Right now, things are in the stratosphere."
The Dow's decline came despite a powerful rally by component Merck & Co. Inc., which surged 8-1/4 to 106-3/4 after reporting strong second-quarter earnings and sales.
The performance was a mirror image of Wednesday's, when the blue-chip average overcame a severe sell-off in component Eastman Kodak Co. after disappointing earnings.
"What we're seeing is investors saying they may sell Kodak because they don't like the earnings or buy Merck because they do," said Richard Cripps chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
"What we're not seeing is evidence that money is leaving the market," he said.
By far the stiffest profit-taking took place in the technology sector, where recent gains have been the most dramatic.

The group may come under new pressure Friday morning, following the release after Thursday's close of Microsoft Corp.'s earnings. Microsoft said it earned 80 cents a share in the quarter, beating Wall Street estimates by a penny.
Analysts said, however, that Microsoft's sprint from a price of 130 to nearly 150 per share in barely a week suggested that the market had expected even better results from the software giant.
"Considering the run we'd seen, coming in at 80 cents when the consensus was 79 cents is not going to do it," said Bill Meehan, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
"This might serve to put some pressure on the market, particularly the large-cap tech stocks," he said.
Microsoft traded lower in after-hours activity, falling to 146 from a closing price of 149-1/2.

Among individual issues, Woolworth Corp. jumped 2-1/2 to 27-9/16 after announcing it would close all its general merchandise stores in the United States, converting some to its more successful speciality athletics format.
The company, named for founder Frank W. Woolworth, also said it plans to change its name later this year.
Raychem Corp. leaped 13-3/8 to 90-1/16 after reporting higher quarterLY earnings late Wednesday.

Louisiana Land & Exploration Co. surged 7-3/8 to 65-5/8. The company agreed to be acquired by Burlington Resources Inc. in a stock deal valued at $3 billion. Burlington Resources fell 1-3/4 to 44-3/8.

Octel Communications Corp. rose 3-3/8 to 30-1/8 after the voice messaging company agreed to be acquired by Lucent Technologies Inc. for $31 per share cash, or $1.8 billion. Lucent, which said it would record an unspecified charge in connection with the deal, fell 2-5/8 to 86-1/16.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 4.98 points to 931.61. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.69 to 637.34.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 2.28 to 482.96. The average share was down 21 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,822.872 down 47.693 or 0.54 percent.
